newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU regional leaders slam Bonn over budget woes.
newsitem.headline: CDU regional leaders slam Bonn over budget woes.

text.p: Several rising stars in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) criticised the beleagured ruling coalition on Tuesday and said it should cut spending rather than raising taxes to fill gaping budget holes.

"The union should propose a consistent course of savings rather than talking about raising taxes," Christoph Boehr, head of the CDU in Rhineland-Palatinate told the Rheinischen Post daily in a release ahead of publication on Wednesday.

Lower Saxony CDU head Christian Wulff, another of the rising generation of CDU politicians dubbed "the young wild things", agreed and said plans by Finance Minister Theo Waigel to solve the budget crisis were a huge danger for the CDU.

Earlier, Waigel was forced to climb down on plans to revalue the currency and gold assets of the powerful Bundesbank which he had hoped would help solve his budget woes and aid Germany's bid to qualify for Europe's single currency.

Head of the Hamburg CDU Ole von Beust told the paper he could not understand why Kohl's CDU and sister party the Christian Social Union (CSU) had not found a solution to their budget problems with junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), who steadfastly oppose tax increases
"The joy of the (opposition Social Democrats) SPD and the Greens over the coalition's policies should give the Bonn coalition parties something to think about," he said.
Head of the Saar CDU Peter Mueller told German radio the coalition was losing the trust of the party grassroots over its plan to revalue the central bank's reserves.
